question_this_answers: For each catalogue category, which attributes are MUST-HAVE: if the product's value differs from what the bike needs, the product is excluded. Everything else ranks.
decisions_already_made: A missing attribute is never a guess: it yields cannot_confirm, not a fit.
Speed count is an exact match, not a maximum (a 2x11 derailleur is not offered for a 2x10 bike).
Max chainring is soft: a shorter cage is compatible_with_calibration, trimmed on the limit screw.
e-bike and e-scooter manuals are excluded; only the two bicycle manuals are sources.

Questions to the rider ARE allowed (supersedes the v0.1 'no questions' decision): at most three per bike, ordered by consequence, options drawn from stock, never a form. A question must resolve one named missing attribute.
A candidate shown alongside cannot_confirm is a LEAD, never a recommendation: the advisor must not render it as a confirmed fit until the missing attribute is supplied.

tier_b.note: wrong size is ugly, not impossible.
9/16in thread is not recorded anywhere - add the attribute before making it a must-have.
lock-on vs slide-on is the only real split.
size is a must-have where present (64%); promote when coverage rises.

open_questions: Pedal thread (9/16in) is recorded on no product: add the attribute before making it a must-have.
Bottom-bracket shell standards (BSA/BB86/BB92/PF30/T47) appear only in the excluded e-bike manual; the bicycle manuals state shell type but not the table.
Rim ERD is not recorded, so spoke length cannot be computed from the catalogue alone.
The bicycle manuals are silent on speed cross-compatibility; shop decision keeps it exact.
22 of 48 front derailleurs have no max chainring value; that rule stays soft and mostly unknown.
